notes.aliyekuja: A relative: a-li-ye-kuja, he or she who came.

guidebook.intro: Eid, Christmas, weddings and graduations bring families together, with plenty of food, music and guests.

tips.title: Who, which: -ye-, -o-
body: To say “who” or “which”, Swahili puts a small marker inside the verb, after the tense: **a-li-ye-kuja** (he or she who came), **wa-li-o-kuja** (those who came).
The marker agrees with the noun: **-ye-** for one person, **-o-** for many, **-cho-** for a ki- thing: **kitabu nilichonunua** (the book I bought).

culture.title: Weddings
body: A coastal wedding can last several days, with women’s celebrations, henna and **taarab** music. Guests are counted in hundreds, and everyone who comes is fed.

culture.title: Holidays for all
body: Kenya and Tanzania keep both Christian and Muslim holidays. Neighbours greet each other with **Sikukuu njema!** at Eid and at Christmas alike, and share food.
